question.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=8-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{x}{4}+5).$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =8-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{x}{4}+5)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =8-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{y}{4}+5).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =8-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{y}{4}+5) \\ -3\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{y}{4}+5) & =x-8 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{y}{4}+5) & =\frac{8-x}{3} \\ {e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(y/4+5)} & ={e}^{(8-x)/3} \\ \frac{y}{4}+5 & ={e}^{(8-x)/3} \\ \frac{y}{4} & ={e}^{(8-x)/3}-5 \\ y & =4({e}^{(8-x)/3}-5) \\ y & =4{e}^{(8-x)/3}-20\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=4{e}^{(8-x)/3}-20.$
